newsitem.title: THAILAND: Soros funds had key role in baht crisis -- newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Soros funds had key role in baht crisis -- newspaper.

text.p: Hedge funds under the control of George Soros played a key role in speculation in the Thai baht in May and have $4 billion in forward currency contracts due in August, The Nation newspaper reported on Monday.
Citing unidentified bank sources, the paper said Soros hedge funds triggered a run on the currency on May 15, taking the baht from 26.00 baht per dollar to 26.70 before buying back the baht at 26.30.
Soros has $4 billion in three-month forward currency contracts due in August and a war-chest totalling $6 billion, the newspaper said.
The Thai baht, which is pegged to a basket of currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar, has come under attack several times recently past as Thailand's economic fundamentals have deteriorated.
The last attack on the baht was in May.
The central Bank of Thailand, with the assistance of other regional central banks, has so far successfully supported the currency.

The Bank of Thailand, which has enacted foreign exchange controls to limit the supply of baht offshore to prevent further attack, is now aiming to strike back at speculators by cutting off their supply of funds to cover forward positions, The Nation said.
The exchange controls, which have seen the baht strengthen sharply offshore, have so far cost some individual speculators $50 million to $60 million, the newspaper said.
